source_file: Berlin 2026 edition for next app devCon 2026 (flutterCon Berlin), sources listed on the page
question: Q5: The Europe Factor

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you have seen a salary range in a Flutter job ad this year.
sections.hint: EU Pay Transparency Directive 2023/970: member states had until 7 June 2026 to transpose it, so ranges in job ads are becoming the norm. Ask whether a range changed a decision.
no_hands: Where do you get salary information today: friends, surveys, recruiters, guesswork?
Would a visible range change which ads you apply to?
For hirers: are you ready to put a range in every ad, and what are you afraid of?
hands_up: Did the range change your decision to apply, or your ask in the interview?
Was the range for Flutter different from the native roles you saw?
Was the range honest, or a wide band that said nothing?
Have you seen ranges more often in Germany, elsewhere in the EU, or in remote roles?
follow_ups: Does transparency help juniors or seniors more?
What should a Flutter developer in Berlin ask for, without naming your own number?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you work for, or hire for, a company in a different country than the one you live in.
sections.hint: Two facilitators, two markets: Berlin and Riga read the same job boards and see different offers. Ask what a portable skill is worth when the team is spread across countries.
no_hands: Would you take a fully remote role from another country, and what would worry you?
Do you think Berlin or the Baltics compete with each other or with the US for Flutter work?
For hirers: what stops you hiring across borders: law, time zones, trust, or tax?
hands_up: How did the cross-border setup happen: remote job, relocation, contractor, employer of record?
Does the framework matter more or less when the team is spread across countries?
What surprised you most: pay, working culture, or paperwork?
Is Flutter a portable skill across markets, or does each market want something else?
follow_ups: Where in Europe is the Flutter demand you actually see?
What would you tell someone in Riga or Berlin who wants to work for a company abroad?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if an EU rule (AI Act, Accessibility Act, GDPR) created a ticket in your backlog this year.
sections.hint: EU AI Act: the AI-literacy duty applies since Feb 2025 and the high-risk rules for hiring tools moved to Dec 2027 (Digital Omnibus, Jul 2026); the Accessibility Act applies since June 2025. Ask which rule became a real ticket.
no_hands: Which rule do you expect to hit your app first, and are you ready?
Is accessibility on your definition of done, or something for later?
For team leads: who on your team knows what the AI Act asks of an app that uses a model?
hands_up: Which rule, what ticket, and how much work was it really?
Did the rule change a design decision or a technology decision?
Was Flutter a help or a hindrance: semantics, screen readers, data handling?
Did anyone budget for it, or did it come out of feature time?
follow_ups: Is regulation a competitive advantage for European developers, or just cost?
What is one accessibility fix every Flutter app in the room could ship this month?

wrap_up: Does being in Europe make Flutter a better or a worse bet than in the US, and why?
Which EU rule will shape your next project more than any framework choice?
